content:
Manuel de Jesús Cruz-Estudillo, 42, the man wanted in the Pueblo Nuevo double homicide, is now in custody, according to KGNS and the Laredo Morning Times. The Webb County Sheriff's Office announced the capture, and KGNS reports Cruz-Estudillo surrendered voluntarily at Bridge No. 1 in Laredo on Tuesday after having fled to Mexico. U.S. Customs and Border Protection took him into custody and processed him, then turned him over to the Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division on two outstanding murder warrants.

The case began the night of Saturday, Oct. 24, in the 800 block of Main Street near Highway 359 in Pueblo Nuevo, where deputies found Gustavo Ramos Moreno, 40, and Raúl Ramos Moreno, 43, with gunshot wounds. Family members said the two men were brothers; one died at the scene and the other died later at a hospital. The Sheriff's Office held a press conference on the case Monday, while the suspect remained at large through Tuesday daytime.

KGNS reports the Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division secured the surrender in coordination with U.S. and Mexican law enforcement. The Laredo Morning Times reports the investigation continues following the capture. KGNS does not report a court date or bond in its custody article.

Webb Watch 956 previously covered the Sheriff's Office search for the suspect in the Pueblo Nuevo double homicide.

Sources:

  • KGNS, "Suspect in custody in Pueblo Nuevo double homicide," by Mariana Flores-Sosa, Oct. 27, 2026
  • Laredo Morning Times, "Pueblo Nuevo double homicide suspect in custody, investigation ongoing," Oct. 27, 2026

title: Pueblo Nuevo double-homicide suspect now in custody after surrender at Bridge No. 1
